newsitem.title: FRANCE: Blockade disrupted Eramet's mines in N. Caledonia.
newsitem.headline: Blockade disrupted Eramet's mines in N. Caledonia.

text.p: A one-day road blockade disrupted production at nickel mines throughout New Caledonia on Monday, including those of Eramet, a company spokesman said on Wednesday.
Pro-independence Kanak Socialist Liberation Front Party (FLNKS) organised the blockade as France is currently holding negotiations over mining reserves in the Pacific territory.
"Our mines did not operate on Monday as road blockades prevented workers from getting to the plants," he told Reuters.
Nickel production resumed on Tuesday at all of Eramet's mines.
The one-day disruption in mineral production is not expected to hurt nickel metal production or sales, the spokesman said.
Eramet produces three million tonnes of nickel ore in New Caledonia each year for a total nickel metal output of some 53,000 tonnes.

Under a 1988 plan to quell separatist tensions in the French territory France has agreed to help rebalance the economic interests of the local Kanak people against those of French settlers ahead of a vote on independence set for 1998.
As part of plan France is widely expected to support a project by pro-independence FLNKS and Canadian metals group Falconbridge to build a nickel plant in the north of New Caledonia.
But the plan would deal a stong blow to Eramet's expansion strategy in New-Caledonia as Eramet might be forced to sell part or all of its Thiebaghi reserves to supply the new plant.
France said on early October it had no plans to strip the mining assets of Eramet in New Caledonia.
